apps.name: Apparition
apps.subtitle: Sideload, sign and refresh apps on the device itself
apps.localizedDescription: Install apps from AltStore-format sources, sign them on the device with a free Apple ID or your own certificate, keep them refreshed, and launch them with JIT.

versions.localizedDescription:
## Fixes

- **JIT for apps inside LiveContainer (#15).** With LiveContainer's JIT enabler set to StikDebug, Launch with JIT now works. A JIT link that names no process now launches the app again under the debugger, as StikDebug does, so LiveContainer starts the app you chose with JIT. Before, Apparition attached to the copy of LiveContainer waiting for it, and the app never got JIT.
- **Stop always ends a JIT session,** including while it is still starting. Before, it did nothing until the debugger had attached.

## New

- **StikDebug JIT scripts.** A script sent with the JIT request (as LiveContainer sends one you added to an app) now runs as the app's debugger. Apparition asks you first every time, because a script can read and change everything in the app.
- **JITProbe**, a minimal test app in the repository: it asks for JIT memory, writes code into it and runs it, and says "JIT works".

Tested on an iPhone 15 Pro Max with iOS 27.0.1 and LiveContainer Nightly, with and without StikDebug's `universal.js`.

## Dependency changes

- **zip 9.1.** Apparition now reads IPAs and `.deb` packages with zip 9.1, which fixes a parsing difference between an archive's two headers (GHSA-m665-v7pm-7grj). That only matters to software that checks an archive with one of the library's readers and extracts it with the other. Apparition uses a single reader for both, so it wasn't affected. Entries whose names can't be decoded are now skipped rather than guessed at.

## Fixes

- **Sign-in "403 Forbidden" (#12).** Some of Apple's `gsd.apple.com` servers refuse sign-in from some networks, depending on your DNS resolver. Apparition now avoids a server that does this for an hour and retries on another one, found through your system DNS or DNS-over-HTTPS. A connection that fails or times out gets one retry on other servers. If every server refuses, the error says Apple turned the network away and what to try.
- **Sign-in status is visible.** The status and its Try again button now appear under the form, and an error scrolls into view, instead of sitting below the fold.
- **Stale Library errors.** Cards now say when the last failure happened ("Failed 2 days ago"), and failures that blame an anisette address are dropped once that address changes.

## New

- **Anisette libraries from a file.** When Apple's download server can't be reached, the desktop app offers Try again and, under Advanced, using Apple Music's libraries from a file. `apparition anisette import` does the same from the command line. Files are checked against the tested version, and a mismatch can be overridden, which is flagged as an unsupported setup. The troubleshooting steps are in the README.
- **Setup badge.** The desktop header always shows where sign-in anisette comes from and what the companion offers.
- **App ID management and reuse.** The desktop app lists your App IDs with quota, expiry, search and deletion. The desktop and native iPhone, iPad, Vision Pro and Apple TV installers share extension selection and App ID reuse. Assignments are saved per team, device and source app, so one registered App ID can serve different apps on different devices.
- **Linux.** Flatpak bundles and direct package downloads.

Windows and the Linux GUI were tested only partly (unit tests and builds). The new sign-in and error handling is covered by unit tests on macOS and Windows.

* Connection: choose Companion or Local VPN, each with its own anisette server. iPhone and iPad can use LocalDevVPN without a computer.
* LiveContainer: export your signing certificate as a .p12 (Settings > Share Signing) for LiveContainer's JIT-less mode. Tested with Delta on iOS 27; see Supported apps.
* Stop: a new Stop button ends a refresh or install at any step.
* Clearer failures: an unreachable anisette server or device says so and offers to retry or switch modes, and a refresh no longer retries a sign-in that already failed.
* Security: rustls is updated for four advisories, and the trusted root CAs drop eMudhra's emSign roots. TLS is what protects the anisette library Apparition downloads.
* Privacy: the Apple ID, team, certificate names, URLs and addresses are kept out of the logs.
* Fixes: a just-installed app is no longer reported missing, Remove from Library works for apps deleted from the Home Screen, and the Share Signing share sheet stays open.

Command line ships inside the Mac app, with apparition link. Choose the signer at install time; data moves when an app changes team. Pairing fails fast, with pairing hand-off, and the device says why it can't be reached.

Apps published as a `.deb` package, such as Kodi, now install. Apparition unpacks the app from the package, so Kodi's official download works as it is. On a Vision Pro, iPhone or iPad, download the `.ipa` or `.deb` in Safari and share it to Apparition, or open it from Files, or use Library > Install from a File: Apparition names the app and asks before installing it. The desktop app (Advanced, An app file) and `apparition install` take a `.deb` too, and a source can list one.

Signing no longer fails on apps that carry object files, which Kodi's bundled Python does (`__LINKEDIT isn't final Mach-O segment`, #7).

A key arriving from another device keeps your Apple ID session, and sign-ins that can't be answered no longer prompt for 2FA. iPhone and iPad build from the main Apparition scheme. The desktop app's window buttons on macOS now line up with the header.
Fixes the Enable JIT prompt on Apple Vision Pro: it opens in its own window in front of you instead of a popover that could land out of reach. Apps only; the desktop installers stay at 0.3.0.

Signing in with the built-in anisette works again. Since 22 October Apple refuses the developer token (-80046) to sign-ins that claim to be an Android phone, which the built-in anisette has to claim, so Apparition now claims a Mac for that one request. Apparition also claims whatever each anisette server reports, so servers that don't run Apple's Android libraries work too.

Your devices now share one certificate instead of making one each. Signing stops before it would make a second Apparition certificate and offers to get the key from the device that has it, nearby over the local network, checked by a six-digit code both screens show: Settings > Get Signing from Another Device and Share Signing with Another Device, Apple TV included. The desktop app and `apparition signing send` and `signing receive` do the same. When the account has no certificate left, Apparition offers this before revoking one, and `apparition signing hand-off` gives the computer's key to an Apparition installed another way.

On Apple TV, free accounts now get a tvOS profile instead of error 8220, Apparition has a home screen icon, and Refresh All is at the top of the Library. Signing refuses an app built for other devices before it uses up one of the week's ten App IDs, and says which version to look for. Adding a source again takes its new options.

Thanks to valentinBoch for the tvOS profile, icon, anisette and isideload 0.5.0 work (#1, #3, #4, #5, #6).

Apparition can now be Madeira's JIT debugger. It answers the links Madeira opens, serves the game for its whole run, and can attach to an app that is already running. While it debugs, Apparition keeps running in the background (silent audio on visionOS, coarse location on iOS) and shows "Debugging Madeira" beside the tabs and in a notification, each with a Stop button. Apps that ask for the increased memory limit get it, along with extended virtual addressing on paid teams.

A new install is now waited for until it finishes; only an update to an app that's open is left queued.

On the command line, `apparition jit` starts or attaches a JIT session and `apparition sign` signs for a paired device without reaching it.

Add sources from a link: an "Add to Apparition" button on a source's page (apparition://source?url=…) opens Add Source with it filled in, ready to add. The desktop app's pairing steps now cover Apple TV too, including the second code it shows for Apparition.

First release. Sideload, sign and refresh apps on the device itself, on Apple Vision Pro, iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, with a free Apple ID (working again after Apple's 12 October change) or your own certificate. The desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux installs it and can stay on as its companion.
